=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** The Seller's note asks us to skip items marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides." Nothing in the package shows Wattlebridge has accepted those positions, so I have reviewed all 16 items. Legal points below (limitation periods, privacy notification, tax survival) need confirmation by NSW/Commonwealth specialist counsel before they go into a mark-up.

**Cross-cutting point:** The known debt-like and specific items total roughly AUD 4.13m before the privacy exposure is quantified: Riverlark ~3.2m, bonuses 0.42m, Ironquay 0.18m, and possibly Sandbar 0.33m. That is close to the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap. These items belong in the price (debt-free/cash-free mechanics) or in specific indemnities, not in general warranty recovery.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, with fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30% (AUD 7.2m) for general warranties, with a fallback no lower than 25%. Reason: known exposures already approach the Seller's cap.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** Claims under AUD 25k are not actionable. A AUD 250k basket applies, and only the excess above it is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10k), aggregation of related claims, and a tipping basket so that once the threshold is crossed the whole amount is recoverable. Fundamental and specific claims should sit outside both.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the excess-only basket; accept a tipping basket with a reduced de minimis. Reason: an excess-only basket leaves the first AUD 250k of loss with the buyer.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, and any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** About 36 months for general warranties, so that an audit cycle and a full FY close are covered. Tax claims should run to the end of the ATO amendment period. Title and capacity should run for the longest available period, commonly six years for contract claims in NSW; confirm this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all claims" default and set survival by category. Reason: a single 18-month period cuts off claims that surface only at the first tax or audit cycle.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties recoverable up to the full price, outside the basket and de minimis, with extended survival.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: the buyer is paying AUD 24m for the shares, and title is what it is buying.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No express fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature" (exclusive remedy, limitations and non-reliance).
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that caps, time limits, thresholds, exclusive remedy and non-reliance do not apply to fraud, including fraud in the disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a fraud carve-out. Reason: as drafted, the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language could bar a fraud claim.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Blanket disclosure of the entire data room to 5.00pm on 22 September 2026 (1.1), plus the accounts, statutory registers and public records (1.2 and Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with matters fairly disclosed against a specific warranty. No deemed disclosure from the data room or public registers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Reason: as drafted, almost every warranty claim could be defeated by something sitting in the data room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion, plus a pro-sandbagging clause confirming the buyer's knowledge does not affect its claims. Known issues should be dealt with through price or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3 and add a pro-sandbagging clause. Reason: combined with 1.1, the clause would exclude every issue the buyer's diligence has identified.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent, treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). The disclosure confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent to Completion requiring an unconditional written consent, or one on terms acceptable to the buyer, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. No waiver by the buyer. If consent is not delivered, a termination right and a specific indemnity or price adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Convert to a condition precedent, not endeavours. Reason: about 30% of revenue is at risk.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl 2/7). The disclosure confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free basis, repayment at Completion out of the price, with discharge of security and PPSR removal delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Repay at Completion through the funds flow. Reason: a post-Completion release leaves the company carrying debt the buyer has paid for.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the draft funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses treated as debt-like or transaction costs and deducted from price, with employer on-costs quantified and paid by the Seller, and the conditions confirmed.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct AUD 420k plus on-costs from price. Reason: the liability is triggered by the company and should not pass to the buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 180k paid before Completion (at the Seller's cost) or deducted from price, a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 IP as a condition precedent, and a specific indemnity for any ownership claim outside the cap, basket and time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Reason: the buyer may not own the IP until payment is made and assignment is documented.

**SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Schedule 6).
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion forensic investigation with a written report; a determination of whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) is triggered; and a specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs, outside the cap, basket and time limits, backed by a retention.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus retention. Reason: the disclosure states the scope and access are unknown and that a download link went to an unintended address. "Not material" is not supported by that record. The notification question is a legal assessment and needs specialist input.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs (DD-008/011).
- **Buyer wants:** A schedule of the contracts showing terms, length, termination rights and change-of-control triggers. Any commitment that is non-terminable, accrued, or triggered by the sale treated as debt-like. Pre-Completion costs borne by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Require the schedule before accepting the ordinary-course characterisation. Reason: the renewals are three related contracts whose timing and scope the disclosure does not settle.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One regime for all claims, with the same caps, time limits and thresholds.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories for general warranties, fundamental and title, tax, specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen, Riverlark) and fraud. Each with its own cap, threshold and survival period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. Reason: it allows the low general cap to govern high-risk known exposures.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the shares.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: a current ASIC company extract, original share certificates, an inspection of the register, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation of no encumbrance. A title warranty and fundamental indemnity from the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. Reason: a register supplied by the Seller is evidence of title but not verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime," meaning the general cap and time limits apply. No tax or IP wording is in the package.
- **Buyer wants:** A tax warranty and pre-Completion tax indemnity in their own category, surviving to the end of the ATO amendment period. IP warranties covering chain of title, including Ironquay, with specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open, not settled. Reason: the package contains no tax or IP drafting, so these cannot be cleared.
